brief.scope: Independently review the supplied test producer record and the resulting tests against the accepted contract and owner input. Static review plus existing producer execution receipts is sufficient; do not invent successful execution if this read profile cannot run Python. Check complete acceptance-row mapping, behavioral discrimination and meaningful red, hermetic state/custody, no weakened existing tests, public-interface assumptions and conformance to admitted boundaries. Refute findings before reporting them; implementation is absent and must not be demanded as test approval. No source/test/contract changes, host state, network or vendor launch. Return inline REVIEW <=1200 words with exact model/ref, approve/changes, precise remaining findings and whether tests are ready to freeze for an independent GPT-6 implementer.

findings.claim: The contract row "rejects duplicate JSON object members" (ops/devlane/task/CONTRACT.md:332-333) is pinned only vacuously. Both string-input tests demand a refusal and no test ever requires a well-formed JSON text to be ACCEPTED, so `def validate_outputs(v, ...): if isinstance(v, str): raise EnvelopeError(...)` turns both green while detecting no duplicate member at all. The pair also silently invents an input polymorphism (validated list OR raw JSON text) that neither ops/devlane/task/CONTRACT.md nor ops/devlane/dispatch/CONTRACT.md declares, and the test itself proves json.loads has already discarded the duplicate (parsed[0]["path"] == "B.md"), so a parsed-data validator cannot honour the row. Needed: either a positive test that a well-formed JSON text of the check-tests array validates to the native list, or move the row to a separate declared text seam (e.g. envelope.load_outputs(text)) with its own accept/refuse pair.

findings.claim: The TypeError fallback (`if "unexpected keyword" in msg or "positional" in msg: return fn(env)`) silently downgrades every declared-outputs call to the historical kwargs-free validate(env). Four of the eight currently green acceptance tests are green only through it, three of them the ones that are supposed to pin the inline exception's narrowness (test_the_exception_does_not_allow_an_inlined_skeptic_report, test_the_exception_does_not_allow_an_inlined_ruling, test_permission_failure_does_not_fall_back_to_inline_without_the_flag): they pass today because envelope._handle (envelope.py:134) already refuses a multi-line handle, with no seam involved. A parameter named differently from inline_planning_exception= therefore produces a scattering of unrelated assertion failures rather than one legible seam refusal. Only test_the_flag_accepts_the_plan_as_an_artifact_string gates the parameter's existence, so the gap is narrow, not open. Needed: assert the fallback was not taken (or skip/fail loudly) in the tests whose subject is the flag.

findings.claim: assertEqual pins TRANSPORT_RESERVED to exactly {COMMIT_MSG, last-message.json}, but both contracts state an open list: "Reserved leaves include last-message.json and COMMIT_MSG" and "The list must include any further transport paths an adapter needs" (task CONTRACT.md:346-348), and dispatch CONTRACT.md:144-150 counts records, session state and supervisor markers as transport. Measured at this ref, launch.py writes only out/last-message.json (499, 818, 957, 1814), out/COMMIT_MSG (1279) and the legacy out/tmp (966) beneath out/, so the two-leaf default is currently correct — but an adapter transport leaf that belongs in the default rather than the reserved= argument would fail a green test and force a test edit by the implementer, who may not make one. Needed: assert containment (issuperset) plus the negative that 'tmp' is absent, which the neighbouring test already covers.
findings.reproduce: grep -n 'Reserved leaves include' ops/devlane/task/CONTRACT.md; grep -n '"out"' ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py

findings.claim: The test calls render_declared_outputs twice with identical arguments (osu.copy_native("check-tests"), osu.OUT_ROOT) and asserts the two results are equal; render takes no job name, so nothing about renaming is exercised and the assertion cannot fail unless the renderer is non-deterministic. It duplicates test_check_tests_renders_the_contract_example_exactly. The contract row (CONTRACT.md:379-380) is genuinely covered elsewhere by test_job_outputs.py:585 test_a_renamed_job_with_the_same_array_is_the_same_declaration, which does vary the name, so this is redundancy rather than a hole. Needed: drop it, or drive it through outputs_from_job for two differently named specs and render both.

envelope.note:
REVIEW — model claude-opus-5 (Opus 5), ref e1745500cecc74b0eb6d9d5c4e548905b8964e5c against 710dbac38c3b187eb4b3302308430c0a6dec4d76. Verdict: changes (1 p2, 3 p3). Not a freeze blocker beyond the p2.

Execution: this read profile CAN run Python, so the producer's receipts were re-measured, not assumed. `python3 -m unittest discover -s ops/devlane/task/tests -p 'test_*.py'` at the reviewed ref: Ran 307, FAILED (failures=86), 0 errors. `-p 'test_job_outputs*.py'`: Ran 94, failures=86, 0 errors, 0 collection failures. 307-94=213 existing task tests, all green — matching record 20260906T102743Z-tests-grok-e05117 exactly (94/86, 213 OK). Per-class static reconciliation also matches its per-file split (55/55, 18/18, 21 with 13 red and 8 green), and the 8 green accept tests are the ones I predicted before running. Diff is 7 files, all `new file mode`, 0 removed lines: no existing test is weakened, deleted or relaxed, and none is edited.

Acceptance-row mapping against ops/devlane/task/CONTRACT.md §C2 (287-448) and dispatch CONTRACT.md §C2 (92-341). Covered with meaningful red: the standalone schema verbatim (array/uniqueItems, file|scratch oneOf, required sets, additionalProperties false, artifact ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$ maxLength 64, $defs.path maxLength 240 and its exact pattern); omission==[] and explicit null refused, both direct and via outputs_from_job; prose never authorizing writes; duplicate paths across kinds, repeated artifact keys, ancestor/descendant overlap, two scratch entries; whole-string grammar including trailing newline, absolute, dot and parent segments, backslash, whitespace, glob, {out} substitution, length bounds; case sensitivity not folded; order preserved; renamed job identity; transport reservations for COMMIT_MSG and last-message.json plus launch-supplied reserved= at equal/ancestor/descendant, with declared scratch tmp explicitly not transport; the byte-exact check-tests, plan and adjudicate sections at /jobs/example/out; JSON string literals with no \/ escaping and lowercase é; the none-grant line; CR/LF strip then two LFs on append; unrepresentable handle refused against envelope.HANDLE_MAX; exact decoded-handle equality with relative, ./, trailing-slash, JSON-quoted, scratch-pointing, wrong-key and missing-key spellings refused; sibling evidence handles permitted; historical records still valid without outputs=; the inline exception not generalized and not an outputs kind. Admitted out of scope and declared as such in the test docstrings, correctly: filesystem custody, digests, attempt provenance, capability witnesses, grant intersection — all dispatch-owned (task CONTRACT.md:428-433, dispatch CONTRACT.md:113-159). test_job_outputs.py is the exact prospective home dispatch CONTRACT.md:336-338 names, and the rows it lists are all present.

Hermetic state and custody: clean. No writes, no tempdir, no env mutation, no network, no vendor launch, no cwd dependence (fixture resolved from __file__); the fixture is one 60-byte file in a new fixtures/job_outputs/ subtree that no other suite enumerates. Reds are AssertionError/assertRaises, never ImportError — outputs_support wraps each absent seam so a missing name fails the contracted assertion instead of erroring the collection, which is the right call and is why 0 errors is reproducible.

Public-interface assumptions: the seams are inventions the contracts do not name — OUTPUTS_SCHEMA, TRANSPORT_RESERVED, validate_outputs (incl. its reserved= keyword), outputs_from_job, render_declared_outputs, append_declared_outputs, and validate(outputs=, out_root=, inline_planning_exception=). That is admissible because the record declares all seven explicitly as p2 missing-seam findings with reproductions, which is what the job asked for; the implementer must match the names exactly and has no other source for them. Refuted as findings, listed here so the freeze is entered knowingly.

Refuted while reviewing: (1) no test asserts a refusal message or a class token — real, but house practice in test_envelope.py is 0 assertRaisesRegex over 18 assertRaises, and the dispatch refusal ids (outputs-schema, outputs-path) are launch-owned, so this is not chargeable here; it does mean launch's id mapping will need its own tests. (2) render raising for an unrepresentable handle looked like task usurping launch's outputs-path admission; CONTRACT.md:432 places representability before child execution and task owns rendering, so it stands. (3) The two-instance envelope load (outputs_support loads it, the other two modules load it again) looked like an identity trap for assertRaises; every assertRaises in those files routes through osu.outputs_error(), so no mismatch today. Worth a comment, not a change. (4) Implementation absence is not demanded as approval anywhere.

Freeze readiness: yes after the p2. Fix test_duplicate_json_object_members_are_refused and its companion test_json_null_text_is_refused — as frozen they let a blanket "refuse any str" satisfy the duplicate-member row without implementing it, and they impose an undeclared list-or-JSON-text input on validate_outputs. That is the one row an independent GPT-6 implementer could pass green while leaving the contract unmet, which is exactly the no-op the contract warns about at CONTRACT.md:210-213. The three p3s are safe to freeze with (they cost redundancy, a possible forced test edit on TRANSPORT_RESERVED, and a slightly less legible failure mode for a misnamed inline parameter), but fixing them now is cheap and keeps the implementer from touching tests they may not approve. Whoever repairs these must not be the implementer.
